description: Migrate EncryptedStorage account-DB encryption from unauthenticated AES-256-CBC to authenticated AES-256-GCM with a versioned envelope, while remaining fully backward compatible with existing CBC-encrypted user databases (read legacy, upgrade-on-write). Resolves SonarQube EncryptedStorage.js:258 (High, Security). This is the highest-risk change and MUST be verified via new and retained tests.
steps: In EncryptedStorage.js sync(): replace the aes-256-cbc write path with aes-256-gcm. Generate a FRESH random 12-byte GCM nonce per write (crypto.randomBytes(12).toString('hex')) - do NOT reuse the persisted 16-byte CBC iv. After encryptTool.final(...), call encryptTool.getAuthTag() and include it. Write a VERSIONED envelope: { v: 2, alg: 'aes-256-gcm', iv: <gcm nonce hex>, salt: this.salt, data: <base64 ciphertext>, tag: <auth tag hex/base64> }. Keep pbkdf2-sha256 / 200000 rounds / DERIVATION_ROUNDS and existing salt handling (this.salt reused across syncs). Keep the atomic tmp-file write + rename logic unchanged.

Because GCM uses a per-write nonce, stop depending on the persisted this.iv for the write path. Keep this.salt (needed for key derivation stability). The _initNewData / _initFreshDatabase iv generation can stay for compat but the GCM nonce for each write must be freshly generated inside sync().

In EncryptedStorage.js _loadExistingFile(): detect envelope version. If input_data has a `tag` (or v===2 / alg==='aes-256-gcm'): decrypt with crypto.createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', derivedKey, Buffer.from(iv,'hex')), call decipher.setAuthTag(Buffer.from(tag, <same encoding used on write>)) BEFORE final(), and let a failed tag throw (caught -> emit 'error', never write). If NO `tag` and it is the legacy {iv,salt,data} shape: decrypt with aes-256-cbc EXACTLY as today so existing DBs still open. Adjust the input validation so a GCM envelope (which still has iv/salt/data) also passes, and a legacy envelope still passes.

Preserve the hard invariant: never write to disk on any decrypt error (wrong password, corrupt ciphertext, bad JSON, missing fields, FAILED GCM AUTH TAG). All failures emit 'error' only. Upgrade-on-write happens naturally: after a legacy CBC file loads successfully, the next sync() writes a GCM v:2 envelope.

Replace the old 'ACCEPTED RISK ... aes-256-cbc' security comment block in sync() with a concise comment describing the new authenticated AES-256-GCM scheme, the per-write random nonce, the versioned envelope, and the legacy-CBC read fallback for backward compatibility.

In test/storage.test.js: KEEP all existing legacy CBC fixture tests unchanged (they prove old data still decrypts - do NOT delete or modify the hard-coded blob/password). UPDATE the 'on-disk format stays {iv,salt,data}' test: new writes now produce a v:2 GCM envelope with additional keys (v, alg, tag) - assert the new envelope shape (contains iv, salt, data, tag, v===2, alg==='aes-256-gcm') rather than exactly ['data','iv','salt'].
ADD test: GCM round-trip (newData, set, sync, reopen with same password -> loaded + data intact + on-disk envelope has tag/v:2).

ADD test: GCM tamper-detection - after a GCM sync, flip/replace a byte in on-disk `data` (or in `tag`), reopen with correct password -> event === 'error' (auth tag verification fails), and file remains byte-identical (no write on error).

ADD test: legacy-CBC -> GCM upgrade-on-save - write the legacy CBC fixture blob to disk, open with 'fixture-password-v1' (loaded), call db.sync(), then read file from disk and assert it is now a GCM v:2 envelope with a tag, AND reopening it with the same password still loads and returns the same data.
acceptance_criteria: New writes produce a { v:2, alg:'aes-256-gcm', iv, salt, data, tag } envelope with a fresh 12-byte nonce per write.
Existing legacy {iv,salt,data} CBC databases still decrypt with the correct password (retained fixture tests pass).
A GCM envelope with a tampered data or tag byte fails decryption and emits 'error' without writing to disk.
Loading a legacy CBC file then calling sync() re-encrypts to GCM v:2 (upgrade-on-write), still decryptable with the same password.
The never-write-on-decrypt-error invariant holds for all failure modes including failed GCM auth tag.
npm test passes with all existing storage tests plus the new GCM tests; total >= 129.
npm run lint clean; node --check EncryptedStorage.js and test/storage.test.js pass.
verification: npm test  (expect all storage tests green incl. new GCM round-trip, tamper-detection, legacy-CBC->GCM upgrade; retained legacy CBC fixture tests still pass)
findings: Migrated EncryptedStorage write path to authenticated AES-256-GCM with a versioned envelope {v:2,alg:'aes-256-gcm',iv,salt,data,tag}. Fresh 12-byte random nonce generated per sync() (24 hex chars) rather than reusing the 16-byte CBC iv; getAuthTag() persisted as hex. Read path in _loadExistingFile detects GCM via presence of tag / v===2 / alg==='aes-256-gcm', calls setAuthTag before final(); legacy {iv,salt,data} envelopes (no tag) still decrypt via aes-256-cbc, upgraded to GCM on next sync(). Field validation unchanged (both envelopes carry iv/salt/data). Never-write-on-error invariant preserved incl. failed GCM auth tag. Tests: updated the on-disk-format test to assert GCM v:2 shape; retained legacy CBC fixture tests unchanged; added GCM round-trip, tamper-detection (data byte and tag byte), and legacy-CBC->GCM upgrade-on-save. npm test 133 pass / 0 fail (was 129). npm run lint clean. node --check passes on both edited files.
